heroHeadline: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey Coordinate Military Response as Houthi Strikes Escalate
heroSubtitle: September brought the sharpest escalation of the war yet: a coordinated Sep 8 Houthi broadside wounded 73 across four Saudi cities and knocked the Jazan refinery offline for a third time, before the Houthis captured the port of Mocha (Sep 10) and seized Mayyun Island and the Hanish Islands (Sep 11), planting their forces directly astride the Bab al-Mandeb Strait for the first time. A Sep 19 ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh — the first strike ever attempted on the Saudi capital — was intercepted at dawn, while renewed Marib fighting through Sep 21 left over 50 Houthi fighters reported killed on the Al-Mashjah and Kahboub fronts. The WHO counted 728 killed or wounded in Yemen since Aug 23, and fighting since Sep 1 has displaced nearly 86,000 people, with Brent crude climbing past $100/bbl for the first time in nearly four months. UN Envoy Hans Grundberg's warning of the highest war risk since the 2022 truce now reads as an understatement.
footerNote: Data sourced from Saudi Press Agency, Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP, Washington Post, Bloomberg, NBC News, CNN, NPR, ABC News (Australia), TASS, Türkiye Today, Anadolu Agency, News.Az, Yemen Monitor, Arab News, UN OCHA, UN News, World Health Organization, Security Council Report, CFR Global Conflict Tracker, Trading Economics, and the US Senate Armed Services Committee record. Contested claims flagged with opposing perspectives.
